slides.title: Welcome to Flexbox & Grid
slides.content:
# CSS Flexbox & CSS Grid 📐

Flexbox and CSS Grid are the twin superpowers of modern web layout design. They replace decades of fragile float and table hacks with robust, flexible, two-dimensional layout systems.

## What you'll master:
- 🔄 **Flexbox Foundations** - Main axis, cross axis, and flex containers
- 🎯 **Alignment & Distribution** - `justify-content`, `align-items`, and `align-self`
- 📏 **Flex Items Sizing** - `flex-grow`, `flex-shrink`, and `flex-basis`
- 🗂️ **CSS Grid Foundations** - Grid containers, track sizing with `fr`, and `gap`
- 🧩 **Grid Template Areas** - Visual ASCII-style page layouts
- ⚖️ **Flexbox vs Grid** - Knowing exactly when to choose which

slides.title: Flexbox Concept: One-Dimensional Layout
slides.content:
# What is Flexbox? 💡

Flexbox (**Flexible Box Layout**) is designed for **one-dimensional** layouts: arranging items along a single axis (either horizontally as a row OR vertically as a column).

```css_not
.flex-container {
  display: flex; /* Activates Flexbox context */
}
```

When `display: flex` is applied to a parent:
1. The parent becomes a **flex container**.
2. All direct children immediately become **flex items**.
3. Children line up horizontally side-by-side in a single row by default!

slides.title: The Main Axis vs Cross Axis
slides.content:
# The Main Axis vs Cross Axis 🧭

Flexbox operates along two perpendicular axes:

```
        ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │                                                        │
MAIN    │   [ Item 1 ]   ───>   [ Item 2 ]   ───>   [ Item 3 ]   │
AXIS    │                                                        │
        └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                    │
                               CROSS│AXIS
                                    ▼
```

- **Main Axis:** Determined by `flex-direction`. Items flow along this axis.
- **Cross Axis:** Runs perpendicular to the main axis.

```css_not
.container {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: row;            /* Main axis is horizontal (default) */
  /* flex-direction: column; */   /* Main axis flips to vertical! */
}
```

slides.title: Justify Content (Main Axis Alignment)
slides.content:
# Aligning on the Main Axis: `justify-content` 🎯

`justify-content` controls how extra space is distributed along the main axis:

```css_not
.container {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: space-between;
}
```

| Value | Behavior |
| :--- | :--- |
| `flex-start` | Items pack against the start (default) |
| `flex-end` | Items pack against the end |
| `center` | Items centered along the axis |
| `space-between` | First item at start, last at end, equal space between |
| `space-around` | Equal space around every item |
| `space-evenly` | Exactly equal space between all items and borders |

slides.title: Align Items (Cross Axis Alignment)
slides.content:
# Aligning on the Cross Axis: `align-items` ⚖️

`align-items` dictates how items are positioned along the perpendicular cross axis:

```css_not
.navbar {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center; /* Centers items vertically when direction is row */
  height: 70px;
}
```

- `stretch` *(Default)*: Items stretch to match the height of the tallest item.
- `center`: Items centered vertically along the cross axis.
- `flex-start`: Items align to the top/start of the cross axis.
- `flex-end`: Items align to the bottom/end of the cross axis.
- `baseline`: Items align according to the text baseline of their content.

slides.title: Centering Everything: The Holy Grail
Flex Wrapping & Spacing (gap)
Flex Items: grow, shrink, and basis
Individual Item Alignment: align-self & order
slides.content:
# Individual Item Control: `align-self` & `order` 🎛️

## 1. `align-self`:
Overrides `align-items` for a specific single item:
```css_not
.special-item {
  align-self: flex-end; /* Pushes just this single item to the bottom */
}
```

## 2. `order`:
Reorders items visually without altering HTML source code:
```css_not
.first-on-mobile {
  order: -1; /* Appears first visually */
}
```

> ⚠️ **Accessibility Warning:** `order` changes visual order only; screen readers still read items in original DOM order.

slides.title: Introduction to CSS Grid
slides.content:
# CSS Grid: Two-Dimensional Layout 🗂️

While Flexbox is one-dimensional (row OR column), **CSS Grid** is **two-dimensional**: it handles rows AND columns simultaneously!

```css_not
.grid-container {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr; /* 3 equal columns */
  gap: 20px;
}
```

## Grid Terminology:
- **Grid Container:** The element with `display: grid`.
- **Grid Track:** A single column or a single row.
- **Grid Cell:** The intersection of a row and a column (like an Excel cell).
- **Grid Area:** A rectangular group of one or more adjacent grid cells.

slides.title: Flexbox vs Grid: The Golden Decision
slides.content:
# Flexbox vs Grid: When to Choose Which ⚖️

Both engines complement each other and are used together in modern applications!

| Feature | Choose Flexbox When | Choose CSS Grid When |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Dimension** | 1D (Row OR Column) | 2D (Rows AND Columns) |
| **Philosophy** | Content-first (items push container) | Container-first (tracks define structure) |
| **Use Cases** | Navbars, button groups, form inputs, toolbars, alignment inside cards | Full-page layouts, photo galleries, dashboards, magazine editorial grids |

> 🎯 **Pro Pattern:** Use **CSS Grid** for the overarching macro page layout, and **Flexbox** inside individual components for micro alignment!

slides.title: Combining Flexbox and Grid
Common Flexbox & Grid Pitfalls
slides.content:
# Common Pitfalls to Avoid ⚠️

1. ❌ **Forgetting `min-width: 0` on flex items:** Flex items have `min-width: auto` by default, which prevents text from truncating with ellipsis (`text-overflow: ellipsis`) unless you set `min-width: 0;` on the flex child!
2. ❌ **Using floats for layouts:** Floats were meant for wrapping text around images in 1996. Never use floats for structural columns!
3. ❌ **Overcomplicating simple 1D lists with Grid:** If you only need a single row of tags or a navbar, Flexbox is simpler and lighter.

slides.title: Summary & Next Steps
slides.content:
# Flexbox & Grid Mastered! 🏆

You have conquered the two most essential layout engines in modern web engineering!

## Key Takeaways:
- ✅ **Flexbox (1D):** Manages flow along the main axis (`justify-content`) and cross axis (`align-items`).
- ✅ **Flex Sizing:** `flex: 1` allows items to grow dynamically into free space.
- ✅ **CSS Grid (2D):** Manages rows and columns simultaneously with `fr` units.
- ✅ **Responsive Magic:** `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr))` creates adaptive layouts without media queries.
- ✅ **ASCII Layouts:** `grid-template-areas` makes entire page templates clean and visual.
